meta.description: Predicts ADMET properties using ADMETlab 3.0 (119 platform features, including 77 prediction models with modeled-endpoint uncertainty), ADMET-AI, DeepChem MolNet, and chemprop D-MPNN with explicit handling of OECD QSAR principles, applicability domain assessment, calibration, hERG/CYP/AMES endpoints, and PAINS / Lipinski / Ro5 / Veber / BBB druglikeness filters. Use when filtering compounds for drug-likeness, prioritizing leads by predicted safety, or building an in-house ADMET QSAR model.

scientific_integrity.detail: Every performance number in the Skill is attributed to a named study and its own benchmark, and the Skill repeatedly refuses to generalise them ('0.956 on their random-split hERG benchmark', 'ADMETlab 3.0 hERG 0.92 (reported)'). The independent external check run here -- ADMET-AI hERG against 300 measured ChEMBL pChEMBL values, AUC 0.711 -- is far below those numbers, which is exactly why the attribution matters and why the Skill's refusal to treat them as general performance is correct.

practice_boundaries.detail: The strongest boundary discipline of any Skill in this audit. Input 6 pushed a 'is this safe to dose' framing and the Skill blocks it at four separate points: a single probability > 0.5 is not a kill signal, important decisions must be confirmed experimentally, ICH S7B/E14 is named as the governing guidance rather than the model output, and it explicitly declines a universal safe/unsafe IC50 cutoff. The word 'patient' appears once, in a cross-reference to a pharmacogenomics Skill; 'prescribe' and 'dose the patient' appear zero times.

methodological_ground.detail: No fallacy. It separates inhibitor from substrate models, warns against counting correlated hosted models as independent evidence, insists PAINS is not a kill filter, requires class-balance reporting for AMES, and states that ensembles give uncertainty but not calibration. Three of these were tested and all three reproduced.

code_usability.detail: The code the Skill ships runs: druglike_score and alerts executed on 300 real compounds, and every function in examples/predict_admet.py parses and executes. The chemprop CLI block trains a real model with the documented flags (verified in the sibling bio-qsar-modeling audit). The defect is coverage, not runnability -- three of the four named prediction tools have no code at all.

functional_suitability.note: The description names four prediction systems. ADMETlab 3.0 (the declared primary_tool) deliberately ships no route; ADMET-AI and DeepChem MolNet appear only in the taxonomy table with no code at all; chemprop gets a commented CLI block. The only executable content is rule-based physchem and RDKit alert catalogs. As a decision document it is excellent; as an ADMET executor it is under-powered.

reliability.note: The per-tool failure-mode section is genuinely strong -- every one of the three tested (OOD chemistry, CYP inhibitor/substrate ambiguity, PAINS as a kill filter) reproduced exactly. Docked because load_admetlab_results enforces no column contract: an unrelated two-column CSV passes, and the instruction to 'preserve the uncertainty columns' has no code or check behind it.

performance_context.note: 299 lines with the depth carried in decision tables rather than prose, and the rule-based path is trivially cheap (300 compounds through druglike_score and three alert catalogs in seconds).

agent_usability.note: Error prevention is outstanding and terminology is consistent. Learnability is docked: the central instruction for the primary tool is 'follow the live official API tutorial', which an agent working offline or against a changed service cannot act on, and no output contract is given to code against.

human_usability.note: The decision-tree-by-scenario table maps directly onto how a project actually asks the question. Docked because a user arriving with 'predict ADMET for my library' gets a document that tells them where to go rather than something that predicts.

security.note: No credentials hard-coded, and the SwissADME entry is notable for treating terms of use as a real constraint rather than an obstacle. Input validation docked for the loader's missing contract.

maintainability.note: Clean separation, and the deliberate refusal to hard-code an unofficial API route is a maintainability decision, not an omission -- it prevents a stale client from shipping. Testability docked: the example's __main__ covers only three trivial SMILES and never touches load_admetlab_results.

agent_specific.note: Escape hatches are best-in-class: four independent statements block a model output from becoming a decision. Composability docked to 3/4 because the ADMETlab route's output contract is undefined, so anything downstream of it is guesswork.

inputs.label: Triage 300 real compounds with the Skill's own druglike_score and alerts snippets
inputs.execution_note: Ran run/analyse_admet.py. Both SKILL.md snippets executed on 300/300 molecules: 196 with zero Lipinski violations, 282 Veber-compliant, 216 passing the BBB simple screen, 92 carrying at least one structural alert across 115 hits (Aliphatic_long_chain 48, Non-Hydrogen_atoms 17). The 3-rule BBB screen scored AUC 0.769 against ADMET-AI's BBB_Martins.
inputs.note: Everything the Skill can execute, executed cleanly. What it produced is a physicochemical and structural-alert profile, not an ADMET prediction.

inputs.label: The ADMETlab 3.0 route -- the Skill's declared primary tool
inputs.execution_note: The documented route could NOT be executed: the Skill deliberately hard-codes no API call ('follow the live official API tutorial') and its code block is a single pd.read_csv of a file the reader is expected to already have. Static evidence was collected instead: examples/predict_admet.py parses and all six functions import; load_admetlab_results raised the documented ValueError on an empty file, returned a DataFrame for a plausible result file, and also accepted a completely unrelated two-column CSV; a missing file gives an unhandled FileNotFoundError.
inputs.note: This is a deliberate design choice by the Skill -- and a defensible one, since hard-coding an unofficial route ages badly -- but it leaves the primary tool with no executable path and no output contract.

assertions.text: The documented ADMETlab route can be executed from what the Skill ships

assertions.note: ValueError('ADMETlab result file contains no predictions')

assertions.text: The loader enforces the column contract the Skill says to preserve

inputs.label: The in-house chemprop D-MPNN route for a custom endpoint
inputs.execution_note: Every flag in the Skill's commented CLI block was checked against chemprop 2.3.1 --help and a real model was trained with them (see the sibling bio-qsar-modeling audit, run/chemprop_train.out): --split-type is a valid alias of --split, v1_rdkit_2d_normalized is a valid featurizer choice, --num-replicates and --ensemble-size exist, and chemprop predict --uncertainty-method ensemble emits an uncertainty column. Scaffold-split test ROC across the four trained models: 0.743, 0.735, 0.776, 0.780. The one flag that does not exist is --seed 42, given in this Skill's Common Errors table: chemprop 2.3.1 offers --data-seed and --pytorch-seed and rejects --seed with 'unrecognized arguments'.
inputs.note: The training route is real and correct. The reproducibility advice in the Common Errors table names a flag the tool does not have.

assertions.text: Every chemprop flag the Skill names exists in the installed release
assertions.note: --seed 42 (Common Errors, 'Predictions inconsistent across runs') is rejected by chemprop 2.3.1; the correct flags are --data-seed and --pytorch-seed

assertions.text: A model trains end to end with the documented flags
assertions.note: 4 models over 2 replicates with v1-equivalent descriptors and a scaffold-balanced split, test ROC 0.735-0.780

assertions.text: Ensemble uncertainty is produced as the Skill claims
assertions.note: chemprop predict --uncertainty-method ensemble wrote a pred_0_unc column

assertions.text: The Skill states that an ensemble gives uncertainty but not calibration
assertions.note: 'Replicates and an ensemble estimator produce an uncertainty estimate, not automatic calibration' -- and it names the separate calibration set that is required

inputs.label: The hERG endpoint checked against 300 measured ChEMBL IC50 values
inputs.execution_note: ADMET-AI 2.0.1 run offline on 300 compounds stratified across the measured pChEMBL range. AUC 0.711 at a pChEMBL>=5 blocker definition and 0.689 at >=6; Spearman correlation with measured potency 0.304. At the Skill's own worked threshold, 293 compounds score above 0.5 and 53 of them have a measured pChEMBL below 5 -- an 18.1% false-kill rate. Tightening to >0.9 still leaves 12.7%.
inputs.note: The single most useful result in this audit: the Skill's central hERG instruction is quantitatively correct on real data.

assertions.note: 300/300 with no failures

assertions.text: The Skill's 'a probability > 0.5 is NOT a kill signal' rule is quantitatively justified

inputs.label: Out-of-distribution chemistry: PROTAC, macrocycles, peptide, metal complex, inorganic salt
inputs.execution_note: Nine probes through the executable route. Sodium chloride received hERG 0.017, AMES 0.672, DILI 0.094, BBB_Martins 0.967, Caco2 -4.518. Cisplatin received AMES 0.905 and BBB_Martins 0.987. The PROTAC-like probe received hERG 0.959 and DILI 0.912; paclitaxel hERG 0.826. The drug controls behaved sensibly (atenolol hERG 0.144, astemizole 0.995). Of the 105 output columns, zero matched any uncertainty, variance, confidence, interval or domain keyword; 52 are DrugBank percentiles.
inputs.note: The Skill names exactly the right chemistry as out-of-distribution, and then prescribes a mitigation that the route it can actually run does not support.

assertions.text: Every out-of-distribution probe received a prediction rather than a refusal
assertions.note: 9/9, including an inorganic salt -- which is the hazard, not the feature

key_strengths: The best practice-boundary discipline in this candidate: four independent structural guardrails stop a model output from becoming a safety decision, and they are embedded in the endpoint guidance rather than bolted on as a disclaimer.

Every failure mode tested reproduced on real data -- the CYP inhibitor/substrate ambiguity on 38% of a 300-compound set, out-of-distribution confidence on metals and peptides, and the PAINS-as-kill-filter trap.
Its central hERG instruction is quantitatively correct: at the threshold it warns about, 18.1% of predicted blockers in a 300-compound external set are measured non-blockers.

It attributes every reported AUC to a specific study and split rather than claiming general performance, which an independent external AUC of 0.711 against reported 0.86-0.956 shows to be the right discipline.
The decision-tree-by-scenario table maps onto how a project actually poses the question, and the chemprop training route it documents trains a working model with the flags as written.

recommendations.title: No executable ADMET prediction route ships with the Skill
recommendations.problem: The description names ADMETlab 3.0, ADMET-AI, DeepChem MolNet and chemprop. ADMETlab is the declared primary_tool and has no request code at all; ADMET-AI and DeepChem appear only as taxonomy rows with no code; chemprop is a commented CLI block. Everything the Skill can actually run is rule-based physchem and RDKit alert catalogs, so the canonical triage produces no ADMET prediction.
recommendations.root_cause: The deliberate and defensible decision not to hard-code a web API route was not paired with an offline fallback, leaving the Skill with no working model path.
recommendations.fix: Add a short executable ADMET-AI section: admet_ai ships its model weights and DrugBank reference set in the package and runs fully offline (verified here: 105 endpoints including hERG, the five CYPs, DILI, AMES, Caco-2 and BBB). Ten lines would give the Skill a working prediction route without touching a network service.

recommendations.title: The prescribed out-of-distribution mitigation is unavailable in the runnable route
recommendations.problem: The OOD and hERG failure modes both prescribe 'check the uncertainty band' and 'if kNN distance to training set > P95, treat as low-confidence'. The only route that can be executed emits neither: zero of 105 output columns carry uncertainty or applicability-domain information, and sodium chloride came back with BBB_Martins 0.967 and AMES 0.905.
recommendations.root_cause: The applicability-domain guidance is written against the hosted service's evidential uncertainty and was never re-grounded in what an offline user can compute.
recommendations.fix: Add a toolkit-independent AD gate the reader can always run: max Tanimoto similarity to a reference set plus a heavy-atom/element sanity filter that rejects inorganics and metals before prediction, with the worked numbers from this audit as the motivating example.

recommendations.title: chemprop reproducibility advice names a flag that does not exist
recommendations.problem: The Common Errors table fixes 'Predictions inconsistent across runs' with `--seed 42`. chemprop 2.3.1 rejects it: 'unrecognized arguments: --seed 42'. The real flags are --data-seed and --pytorch-seed.
recommendations.root_cause: The flag is carried over from chemprop 1.x, which the Skill elsewhere correctly flags as a breaking API change.
recommendations.fix: Replace with `--data-seed 42 --pytorch-seed 42` and note that the two control different sources of randomness. The identical error appears in chemoinformatics/qsar-modeling and should be fixed in both.

recommendations.title: load_admetlab_results enforces no column contract
recommendations.problem: The loader checks only that the file is non-empty. A two-column CSV with a single unrelated field passed unchallenged, and a missing file produces an unhandled FileNotFoundError. The Skill's instruction to 'preserve the uncertainty columns and task identifier' therefore has nothing enforcing it.
recommendations.root_cause: The function was written as a thin wrapper around read_csv for a route whose output shape the Skill declines to specify.
recommendations.fix: Have the loader take a required-columns argument (defaulting to a smiles column plus at least one uncertainty column), raise a named error listing what was missing, and catch FileNotFoundError with a message pointing at the API step that should have produced the file.

recommendations.title: ADMET-AI version pin is two major versions behind the Skill's own warning
recommendations.problem: Version Compatibility pins 'admet-ai 1.3+', while the taxonomy table itself warns that 'v2 package predictions differ from the v1 paper/server'. The installed release is 2.0.1, so the pin admits precisely the version the Skill says will disagree.
recommendations.root_cause: The pin was written as a lower bound before the v1/v2 divergence note was added, and the two were never reconciled.
recommendations.fix: State the tested major version explicitly and repeat the divergence warning in Version Compatibility, not only in the taxonomy table.
